passage:
Students measured river temperature at different points. Water near shaded areas was cooler. Water near concrete banks was warmer.
A biologist explained that temperature affects fish and insects. Warmer water holds less oxygen and can stress some species.
The class planted small trees along a section of the river with permission from the city.
They learned that shade is not only comfortable for people. It can be part of river health.
The project changed how students saw trees near water. They were not decorations. They were quiet climate tools, helping life below the surface.
